props.covers: The arrows block is compact descriptive notation: one from > to line per connection, by reference number, conventionally placed last. It names connection intent; the production router chooses the route, steered when needed with anchors, endpoint positions, and waypoints.

text.insert: at the left margin, then one indented line per connection:
, by reference number. Duplicates are allowed (the document may have them) and order follows the document. An empty block is the bare
header. By convention, this descriptive block appears last.

The from > to lines do not encode bends. On the live board, the production router computes the path. Steer minimally and in order: try an endpoint anchor, then an endpoint position, then waypoints when the corridor demands them. For each connection a batch touches, the ROUTES block reports the true polyline and names every box it crosses in through. Label the edge directly, enter and exit on faces that follow the flow, and keep separate runs from sharing a line. When a route detours or hugs a frame, open the corridor before adding steering.
